module.title: Unit 8: Sporting Moments: Sports, Rules & Modals of Advice
module.objective: Describe sporting events, competition rules, and give advice or recommendations using 'should' and 'shouldn't'.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Famous Sporting Moments
subModules.theme: Sporting Moments: Sports, Rules & Modals of Advice
subModules.grammarFocus: Past Continuous vs Past Simple & Modals of Advice

content.summary: Welcome to the reading mission on famous sporting moments. In this lesson, you will read about incredible stories of athletes, dramatic races, and unexpected events during competitions. You will also learn how to use the past continuous tense to describe actions happening at a specific moment in the past, and review useful language for sports training.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Past continuous (was/were plus verb-ing) for background actions, contrasted with past simple for completed actions.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Sports nouns, athlete equipment, race verbs, and injury vocabulary.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts for specific names and dates, and skimming paragraphs to understand the general story before answering questions.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 reading passages about sports history.
Locate specific details such as athlete names, injuries, and race results.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with the past continuous and past simple.

contextWarmup.prompt: When you watch a sports competition on television, what do you usually notice first?
options: The dramatic moments when athletes overcome injuries or unexpected challenges
Only the final score at the very end of the match
The commercial advertisements shown during the half-time break
contextWarmup.explanation: Sports stories often become famous because of the dramatic human perseverance shown on the field, not just the final score.

rules: Past Continuous: Use was or were plus a verb ending in ing to describe an action that was in progress at a specific time in the past.
Past Simple vs Past Continuous: Use the past continuous for a long background action and the past simple for a short action that interrupts it.
When and While: Use when before a past simple clause and while before a past continuous clause.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Confusing Past Continuous and Past Simple
commonTrap.explanation: Students often use the past simple for everything in a story, but you need the past continuous to show that an action was ongoing when another event happened.
commonTrap.wrong: Derek ran when he felt a sudden pain in his leg.
commonTrap.correct: Derek was running when he felt a sudden pain in his leg.

items.exampleSentence: The British athlete Derek Redmond was a top runner.
The race began, and at first, Derek was running well.
Mountaineer Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner was trying to climb K2.
What do we call someone who does gymnastics?
He felt a pain in his leg and fell down on one knee.
He had a bad injury and could not carry on.
Derek walked the last fifty metres and crossed the line.
He won the bronze medal in the marathon.
The referee blew the whistle to stop the match.
Athletes need hard training every single day.

paragraphs: Sports history is full of emotional moments that people never forget. One famous story happened at the 1992 Olympic Games in Barcelona. A British athlete named Derek Redmond was running in the 400-metre semi-final race. Thousands of fans were watching him closely because he was running very well and had a great chance of winning a medal.

Suddenly, halfway through the race, Derek felt a terrible pain in his right leg. He fell down hard onto the track. It was a severe injury to his hamstring. Medical staff rushed toward him with a stretcher, but Derek refused to give up. He stood up on one leg and started to walk. His father ran down from the stands, put his arm around Derek, and helped him cross the finish line together while the entire stadium stood up and cheered.

questions.question: What event did Derek Redmond participate in at the 1992 Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: The passage states Derek Redmond was running in the 400-metre semi-final race in Barcelona.

questions.question: What was happening just before Derek felt pain in his leg?
options: He was sitting in the stands
He was talking to the referee
questions.explanation: The text mentions he was running very well and had a great chance before the injury occurred.

questions.question: Where did Derek feel the terrible pain?
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states he felt a terrible pain in his right leg.

questions.question: What did Derek do after he fell down on the track?
options: He stood up and walked to finish the race
He got into an ambulance immediately
He stayed on the track until the race ended
questions.answer: He stood up and walked to finish the race
questions.explanation: Despite his injury, Derek stood up on one leg and walked to cross the finish line.

questions.question: Who helped Derek cross the finish line?
questions.explanation: His father ran down from the stands and put his arm around Derek to help him.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence using the past continuous tense.
options: Derek was running when he felt pain
Derek ran when he was feeling pain
Derek runs while he was falling
questions.answer: Derek was running when he felt pain
questions.explanation: Past continuous (was running) describes the background action, and past simple (felt) describes the interrupting event.

questions.question: Which word from the passage means a physical harm or damage to the body?
questions.explanation: An injury is physical damage, such as the severe problem Derek had with his leg.

questions.question: How did the crowd react when Derek and his father crossed the finish line?
questions.explanation: The passage notes that the entire stadium stood up and cheered for them.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: While the athletes ________, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: The word while is followed by the past continuous tense (were training) for an ongoing background action.

questions.question: What is the main message of this reading passage?
options: Determination and support matter more than winning a gold medal
Athletes should never participate in the Olympic Games
Running is the easiest sport in the world
questions.answer: Determination and support matter more than winning a gold medal
questions.explanation: The story highlights human perseverance, family support, and finishing what you start despite adversity.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Sporting Opinions and Rules

content.summary: This listening mission focuses on catching main ideas and specific details when friends discuss sports preferences, personal feelings, and helpful advice. You will practice identifying weak forms in connected speech and listening for key opinion phrases.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about sports preferences.
Identify specific details such as reasons why someone likes or dislikes an activity.
Notice how words link together naturally in fast spoken English.

keyPhrases.note: Used to ask for someone's personal opinion or feelings on a topic.
Used to politely express mild dislike or lack of interest in an activity.
Used to give friendly advice or recommend an action.
Used to show enthusiastic agreement or strong interest in a suggestion.

connectedSpeech.note: The final consonant sound of feel links smoothly to the vowel sound of about.
The hard k sound at the end of like connects directly to the article a.
The verb try links to the pronoun it without any pause between them.
In fast spoken English, the auxiliary verb do and pronoun you blend into a weak sound.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Sporting Moments and Rules

content.summary: Practical guide on sentence structure, sports collocations, and past continuous actions in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Sports Collocations
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + play/go/do + sport or activity + time phrase
blueprintItems.example: Liam plays football every Saturday morning.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Past Continuous for Background Actions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + was/were + verb-ing + when + Past Simple action
blueprintItems.example: The team was running on the track when it started to rain.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Combining Clauses with While and When
blueprintItems.formula: While + Past Continuous clause, + Past Simple clause
blueprintItems.example: While Sarah was practicing tennis, her coach arrived.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize the first letter of sentences, names of people, and days of the week.
mechanicsRules.why: Names and days of the week are proper nouns requiring capital letters.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use correct sports verbs with sports nouns.
mechanicsRules.why: Team sports with balls use play, sports ending in -ing use go, and individual fitness activities use do.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place commas correctly when starting a sentence with While.
mechanicsRules.badExample: While the match was starting the fans cheered.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: While the match was starting, the fans cheered.
mechanicsRules.why: A comma separates the dependent time clause from the main clause.

sampleSentences.en: David was running on the field when he lost his shoe.
sampleSentences.id: David sedang berlari di lapangan ketika dia kehilangan sepatunya.
sampleSentences.focus: Past continuous and past simple with when

sampleSentences.en: While the players were resting, the coach gave important advice.
sampleSentences.id: Saat para pemain sedang beristirahat, pelatih memberikan saran penting.

sampleSentences.id: Emma melakukan senam tiga kali seminggu di gimnasium lokal.

sampleSentences.en: We should always follow the referee rules during a match.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following affirmative sentence into a negative sentence using the past continuous tense:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The players were practicing their moves in the gym.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change were to were not or weren't.
targetAnswers: The players were not practicing their moves in the gym.
The players weren't practicing their moves in the gym.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To form the negative in past continuous with plural subjects, use were not or weren't followed by the verb-ing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct conjunction (when or while):
practicumQuestions.promptText: Anna was stretching before the race, her coach checked the stopwatch.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the conjunction that introduces a continuous background action.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use while directly before a past continuous clause indicating a background action.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with correct capitalization and punctuation:
practicumQuestions.promptText: alex was playing tennis on thursday afternoon
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the name Alex and the day Thursday, and add a period.
targetAnswers: Alex was playing tennis on Thursday afternoon.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Names of people and days of the week must always be capitalized, and sentences need a final period.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the past simple sentence into the past continuous tense using the pronoun He:
practicumQuestions.promptText: He ran across the running track.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use He was followed by the -ing form of run.
targetAnswers: He was running across the running track.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The past continuous is formed with was or were plus the verb-ing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct sports verb (play, go, or do):
practicumQuestions.promptText: My brother likes to swimming at the sports center every weekend.
practicumQuestions.hint: Activities ending in -ing use this specific verb.
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use go with sports and activities ending in -ing, such as swimming, running, and cycling.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with when or while:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The referee blew the whistle the two players were arguing.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the conjunction that connects a short action to an ongoing background action.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use when before a past simple action that interrupts or happens during a past continuous background action.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Form a yes/no question in the past continuous from this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: You were watching the football match.
practicumQuestions.hint: Put Were at the beginning of the sentence.
targetAnswers: Were you watching the football match?
practicumQuestions.explanation: To make a past continuous question, invert the subject and auxiliary verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with a modal of advice (should or shouldn't):
practicumQuestions.promptText: Football players respect the referee decisions during a tense match.
practicumQuestions.hint: Think about what good athletes are advised to do.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Should is used to give positive advice or state proper rules of conduct.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the spelling and grammar error in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: the basketball team were train hard yesterday afternoon.
practicumQuestions.hint: Check the verb form after were.
targetAnswers: The basketball team were training hard yesterday afternoon.
The basketball team was training hard yesterday afternoon.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In past continuous, the verb must take the -ing form. Also, capitalize the first letter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Choose the correct verb (play, go, or do) to complete the sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Emma and her friends basketball in the school yard after classes.
practicumQuestions.hint: Team sports with a ball use this verb.
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use play with team sports and games that involve balls, such as basketball, football, and tennis.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Sporting Moments, Rules and Advice

content.summary: This guide helps you speak clearly about sports events, describe actions using past continuous and past simple tenses, and give advice using modal verbs.
content.audioGuidance: Pay attention to sentence stress when giving advice with should and must. Keep your voice steady when describing past sporting moments.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear short and long vowels in sports vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Pronounce vowels distinctly in words like athlete, race, and medal so listeners understand you clearly.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.target: Stress key words in modal advice sentences
pillars.explanation: Emphasize modal verbs like should and must when giving important sports rules or safety advice.

pillars.name: Intonation
pillars.target: Use falling intonation for statements and rising intonation for questions
pillars.explanation: Lower your voice at the end of completed thoughts about past races and injuries.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the main stress shifts from the first syllable to the second syllable.
The stress moves between the first and second syllables depending on the word form.
The main stress moves to the middle syllable when adding suffixes.
Longer compound words shift the primary stress towards the end.
